# Anna v6 matcher regression evidence

`dev-baseline.json` preserves the original Anna create request, the pre-correction DEV catalogue (`snap_00e8f4311baa16a3`), and its applicable safety-reference snapshot from 7 September 2026. It includes all 154 seller listings / 79 products. Product identities, prices, physical metadata, facts, confidence, source evidence, and reference versions are unchanged. Its provenance records the original capture's SHA-256 and deployed source commit.

This is a historical input fixture, not the corrected production catalogue. Do not update it when catalogue corrections deploy. `ANNA6-RETAIL-01` evaluates the reported create and objective-only revision using the maintained production request normalizer, bridge, shared matcher and public projection. It asserts productive choices, honest unknown pill counts, context preservation, actual expansion evidence, and frozen line prices. It does not claim the bounded search found a global optimum. The same regression fails against the pinned a659a229 source because the original result has no purchase choice.

## Intentional maintained-expectation changes

These changes replace numeric eligibility vetoes with the approved v6 advisory behaviour. Historical QA results and the v5 expectation-change ledger remain intact. No fixture prices or original case IDs were changed.

| Maintained case | Replaced expectation | Required replacement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `WEB5-02` | Zero/one product ceiling truncates a basket | Both preferences retain all eight independently required products |
| Web adapter compact/balanced comparison | Compact three-product ceiling forces a different result | Both expose the four-product exact fit and full coverage |
| Dose-fit known-food candidate coverage | Pill ceiling prevents a target-covering quantity | Supported quantities can meet the target above the preference; total versus supplemental reference arithmetic remains asserted |
| Dose-fit one-pack pricing | Budget one minor unit below price rejects the pack | Same supported quantity, exact fit and unchanged 48,500 pack price |
| Dose-fit distinct-pack pricing | Budget one minor unit below subtotal removes one product | Both packs remain, with exact doses and unchanged 58,500 subtotal |
| Dose-fit country/frontier case | Pill preference removes the unique cheap exact fit | Exact two-pill product wins at price 10; foreign seller remains ineligible and frontier members must contribute |
| `V5-COUNT-02` | Explicit zero/one ceiling is enforced | One-target basket remains one product; two-target basket remains two products at zero/one preference |
| `V5-DOSE-05` | Proposed product conflicts with product-count preference | Physically supported proposal remains valid; unsupported splitting and excluded proposals still fail |
| `V5-REPAIR-01` | Three-pill veto makes a three-product combination the unique optimum | Supported ten-unit quantities retain the cheaper exact two-product fit (price 200, 20 pills) |
| `ADV6-REPAIR-01` (additional) | Complementary repair formerly exercised using the pill veto | Original three-product combination is still found at exact one-unit product proposals (price 300, three pills) |
| Phase3 single-SKU budget case | Product rejected for budget | Exact SKU remains at its original 16,000 price and zero dose loss |
| Phase3 heavy-SKU pill case | Eight-pill serving rejected | Supported eight-pill exact dose remains at its original 16,000 price |
| `M-06` | One-product ceiling forces partial coverage | Same full-dose option as unrestricted search; high-dose trap stays excluded from the recommendation |
| Independent tiny arithmetic loop | Skip every basket above three pills | Enumerate the declared finite 0–4 quantity grid without a pill-preference filter; preserve independent exact arithmetic and objective checks |

Additional maintained regressions cover numerical-preference invariance, retained-product reservations, fixed proposals, categorical constraints, unknown-pill total ordering and safe dominance, an independent finite oracle, mandatory-question/readiness removal, actual diagnostic counts, and localized web preference disclosure. Stronger pill ordering distinguishes unknown from measured zero without adding dose-fit weights.

Follow-up inventory replacements preserve the P1 request's 39,000-minor-unit goods price while testing advisory budget updates, locale changes and clearing; Phase2 pill/budget cases now require the same evaluated closest fit above the preference and reject false hard-constraint certificates. The v5 conversational journeys preserve exact current-intake/no-purchase and fallback selection checks while asserting the new trace-backed `targets_already_covered` and `empty_closest_fit` explanations. Retention tests distinguish preserving a product/nutrient identity from imposing a numerical target amount.

`legacy-v5-six-product.json` was generated by the unchanged a659a229 implementation from the existing eight-target legacy test request and original SKU prices. It captures the v5 six-product computation plus its persisted checkout operations. SHA-256: `46de316fa5cdce9b0e5d055af6c81af9875f59025da8b4c43e889f0625a56424`. Its capability key, handles, payment adapter and identities are synthetic test fixtures. The tests replay only those in-memory persistence operations and keep a fixed fixture clock. No provider or database is involved.

LEGACY5-02 now verifies that an explicitly supplied six remains available for advice while a refreshed exact-fit basket may contain eight products. LEGACY5-05 continues to require exactly six frozen line items, unchanged quantities/prices/payment identities, and recovery for both paid and unpaid historical checkouts. Historical fixture creation is never rerun through the current matcher.

`DEV-SAFETY-01` and `DEV-SAFETY-03` now look up the explicitly published reference scope instead of assuming supplemental scope after its retirement. They require a real matching ledger, its rule ID/version, a returned limit and correct unit conversion. The previous vacuous `SAFETY-03.notHardcoded` expression and nullable success paths are replaced with these provenance and arithmetic assertions; clinical limits are not changed by the tests.
